newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: Swiss bond market closing report.
newsitem.headline: Swiss bond market closing report.

text.p: Swiss bonds turned in a mediocre performance despite strong gains in German and U.S. bonds, leaving some dealers here perplexed.

"The performance in the Confederate bond futures contract was disappointing," said one, adding he believed one large Swiss bank may have been aggressively selling Conf contracts into the market's rise on Wednesday.
He added such selling may have been tied to a recent rash of new issues, with some perhaps still be waiting to be placed.
The Swiss federal government also holds an auction on May 22.
Recent new issuers include the Canton of Lucerne, Swiss grocery chain Migros, and Finland.
The trader added 'end-investors' -- retail and institutionals -- appeared to need new bonds, but the outstanding supply was likely sufficient.
At the same time, market makers probably have covered shorts, but may not be long.
"It is a bit of a neutral zone," the trader said.
He believed that at 120.00 on the June contract some participants could turn to sellers. The June Conf ended near its high of 120.40 compared with the low of 120.20.
Conf futures CONFc1 up nine at 120.38.
Comi medium-term bond COMIc1 up seven at 111.70
Euro Swiss francs FESc1 up two at 98.20.
